sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- Anjali Upadhya,C.S.C.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ashish Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Ambrish Shukla,
learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Mrs. Anjali Upadhyay,
learned counsel for the respondent Nos.2 to 4 - Greater NOIDA Industrial Development Authority.

2. The present writ petition is preferred praying inter alia with the following relief:
"i. Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction commanding respondent nos.2 to 4 to allot land to petitioner in exchange under the lease-back policy of the Greater Noida Development Authority.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction commanding respondent nos. 2 to 4 to decide the representations given by the petitioner with speaking order."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner, along with one Ram Kishan Yadav,
purchased 0.1450 hectares (1450 square meters) in Khasra No. 271, Khata No. 79 situated in the village of Roja Yakubpur through a registered sale deed dated01.05.2007 from its erstwhile owner Brijesh Yadav.
Post- purchase
, the petitioner's name was duly mutated in the revenue records.

He states that thereafter acquisition proceedings were commenced and the notification under Section 4 read with Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1984')
was published/ gazetted on 31.08.2007.
This was followed by a notification on 27.02.2008 under Sections 6(1) read with Section 17(4) of the Act, 1894 and award was made on 29.11.2010.
Learned counsel for the petitioner in this backdrop states that it is not in dispute that the award was made but till date the petitioner has not lifted the award compensation.

He submits that a decision by the constituted committee on 10.05.2013 approved on January 07.01.2014, resolved to allot land under the lease-back policy equivalent to 50% of the petitioner's land in Arazi No. 271, area 725 square meters, recognizing existing constructions under the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority Rural Abadi (Management and Regularization) First Amendment Regulations 2013.

entities.text: Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority Rural Abadi (Management and Regularization) First Amendment Regulations 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this backdrop, he submits that on 15.11.2018, the development authority decided to return the land through lease execution to the owner.
The petitioner has consistently represented to the development authority for the return of land under the lease-back policy, submitting a representation on 12.07.2021.
Despite another representation on 17.01.2022, no action was taken.

The petitioner later discovered the authority had allotted plots under its scheme for 5% developed land from his acquired land in Khasra No. 271, prompting another representation on 29.12.2023, for the return of his 725 square meter land as per the lease-back plan.
Despite persistent efforts, the petitioner's grievances remain unresolved, as the respondent authorities have not allotted land as per the scheme, seemingly for extraneous reasons.
Such situation has impelled the petitioner to prefer the writ petition for the aforesaid relief.

4. Per contra, Mrs. Anjali Upadhya, learned counsel for the Greater NOIDA Industrial Development Authority states that so far as the release of land is concerned, the same cannot be pressed before the competent authority, i.e. the State Government as the policy is of the year 2017 and thereafter,
the claim of the petitioner has been rejected on 15.11.2018.
She submits that in case the petitioner is inclined to lift the award compensation, he is at liberty to approach the SLAO.
In lieu of the award, if the lease back policy is still in existence, the claim of the petitioner would be considered in accordance with law.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as the relief as has been prayed for, the authority has not passed any order, we dispose of the writ petition with an observation that the Chief Executive Officer may take a final call on the representation of the petitioner in accordance with law expeditiously, preferably within six weeks from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order.
